explainBack.q: Some people say Tailwind is just inline styles. Using your page, explain why it isn't.
lookFor: consistent design scale (spacing/colours)

explainBack.q: How does Tailwind keep the final CSS file small?

only generates used classes

lastHintExplanation: Inline styles can't do hover, focus, media queries or dark mode, and they don't follow a design scale. Tailwind classes are a fixed scale (p-4 is always 1rem) with variants like md:, hover: and dark:. Tailwind scans your source files and generates CSS only for the classes you actually use, so the final file stays small.

predict.why: Tailwind scans for complete class names; it can't run your code to build strings.

Angular reuses DOM for items with the same id

title: Signals: signal, computed and effect
goal: Manage component state with signals so the UI updates automatically and efficiently.

concepts: signal(initial): read with count(), write with set() and update()
Never mutate a signal's object/array in place; create a new one
computed(() => ...) for derived values (cached, recalculated when dependencies change)
effect(() => ...) for side effects like saving to localStorage
Why signals: Angular knows exactly what changed
Reading signals in templates: {{ total() }}

build.task: Refactor course-list to signals: courses = signal<Course[]>(...), query = signal(''), and levelFilter = signal<'all' | Level>('all'). Make filtered and savedCount computed signals. Toggle saved with courses.update(list => list.map(...)) (no mutation). Add an effect that saves saved course ids to localStorage, and load them in the initial signal value. Then build a separate cart component: items signal, computed subtotal, GST (18%) and total, quantity +/− buttons, and remove; all updates immutable.
acceptance: State in signals; filtered and savedCount are computed
No in-place mutation of signal values (no push, no item.saved = ... on existing objects)
effect persists saved ids; they survive a reload
Cart totals always correct after +, − and remove; quantity can't go below 1
Templates call signals as functions: {{ total() }}

hints: Toggle: this.courses.update(list => list.map(c => c.id === id ? { ...c, saved: !c.saved } : c)).
computed reads other signals: filtered = computed(() => this.courses().filter(c => c.title.toLowerCase().includes(this.query().toLowerCase()))).
effect must be created in an injection context. Declaring it as a class field (persist = effect(() => ...)) or in the constructor works.

explainBack.q: Why must you create a new array/object instead of mutating inside a signal?
lookFor: signals notify when set to a new value
same reference means no change detected
computed won't recalculate

explainBack.q: When does your computed total recalculate, and when doesn't it?
lookFor: when a signal it reads changes
cached otherwise
only reads dependencies it used

explainBack.q: What's the difference between computed and effect?
lookFor: computed returns a derived value
effect runs side effects
don't set signals in effect normally

lastHintExplanation: A signal notifies its readers when you set() or update() it to a new value. If you mutate the existing array, the reference doesn't change, so computed values and the template aren't told anything changed. computed derives a cached value and recalculates only when a signal it read changes. effect runs side effects (like saving) whenever its signals change.

predict.q: items = signal([1, 2]); total = computed(() => items().length); items().push(3); console.log(total())
predict.why: push mutates without notifying, so the cached computed isn't recalculated.
